target_customer: Trucking fleets and freight railroads whose exhaust is captured; captured CO2 is sold to industrial buyers such as concrete producers, beverage makers and greenhouses
problem: Heavy-duty diesel trucks and locomotives are hard to electrify, so their CO2 is emitted at scale. Remora captures it onboard and sells it, sharing revenue with the vehicle operator.
business_model: Hardware device on vehicles plus sale of captured, purified CO2, with revenue shared with fleet or railroad customers

founders.name: Paul Gross
education: Yale University (senior year when he read the CTO's dissertation, per the Launch HN post)
founders.background_notes: YC page bio says he ran large-scale randomized experiments on political participation before Remora and cycled across the US before college. Wrote the business plan that persuaded the CTO to leave the EPA.

founders.name: Christina Reynolds
prior_employers: US EPA (left to start Remora, per Launch HN)
education: PhD, testing adsorbents for CO2 capture from diesel exhaust
founders.background_notes: Remora technology originated from her doctoral dissertation (Carbon Herald, Launch HN).

founders.name: Eric Harding
founders.background_notes: Launch HN says he previously built hydrogen and electric semi trucks. Full surname seen only in a secondary profile, not on the YC page.

competitors.name: CarbonCure
competitors.what: Injects captured CO2 into concrete; named in the launch thread as a leader in CO2 utilization, so an adjacent buyer or substitute outlet rather than a mobile capture rival

competitors.name: Solidia
competitors.what: CO2-cured concrete technology, named alongside CarbonCure in the launch thread as adjacent

technical_complexity.rationale: Onboard adsorbent capture on a moving truck, purification of exhaust CO2 to usable grade, and integration with semi trucks, with the core method coming from a PhD dissertation and no published precedent cited by commenters in 2021.

defensibility.rationale: Patentable adsorbent and device know-how from the CTO's research and hardware complexity slow copying, but the sorbent chemistry is studied widely and the customer lock-in is modest.

incumbents: Oil majors with carbon capture programs
takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent was reported copying or buying Remora through the 2025 Series B; rail partners signed pilots with Union Pacific and Norfolk Southern in 2025 per press.

market_need_then: Heavy-duty trucking was a large and hard-to-electrify emissions source, and the launch post pitched battery and hydrogen trucks as impractical for long haul. A buyer base for CO2 existed in concrete and beverages, though no 2021 demand figures were found.

branding.name_origin: Secondary profiles say it is named after the remora fish that attaches to a shark, mirroring a device that attaches to a truck; the company site does not explain it.
branding.domain_note: Company uses remoracarbon.com, not remora.com; legal entity is Echeneidae Inc.

identity.visual_style: Industrial hardware imagery, images of the unit at its Wixom, Michigan facility

branding.brand_signature: The remora fish metaphor of riding along on existing vehicles and infrastructure
branding.community_and_virality: Press coverage in WSJ, Greenbiz and Fast Company is linked from the YC page; no merch or fan community found.

brand_strength.rationale: A memorable nature metaphor and notable press, but no evidence the brand itself drove growth; the domain carries a carbon suffix.

pivots.to: Tender-based capture for diesel locomotives plus trucks
pivots.why: Rail partnerships with Union Pacific and Norfolk Southern announced in 2025 per press; the company says it now serves trucks and locomotives

outcome_analysis: Remora launched in Winter 2021 with a research-based device for capturing truck exhaust CO2 and has stayed active, reaching about $117 million raised by April 2025 including a $60 million Series B led by Valor. Its success so far rests on a hard technical asset from the CTO's research and climate investor backing, while commercial scale is unproven in public sources and the 2025 shift to locomotives suggests the truck wedge widened rather than narrowed.
notes: Earlier rounds are reported inconsistently: Dealroom lists a $37M Series A in March 2023 led by Lowercarbon and a $60M round in June 2023, while Carbon Herald dates the $60M Series B to April 2025 and gives total funding of $117M. These earlier figures are from aggregators and left out as unverified. The YC page says over $115M raised. The shard description mentions beverage grade CO2 for breweries and greenhouses, matching the company's later positioning. No layoffs or shutdown found; one low quality blog speculated about quiet in 2026 without evidence.
